definitions.explanation: A set of seven edible wild plants traditionally eaten in rice porridge on January 7th ({七草|ななくさ}の{節句|せっく}) to pray for good health in the new year. The seven herbs are: せり (water dropwort), なずな (shepherd's purse), ごぎょう (cudweed), はこべら (chickweed), ほとけのざ (henbit), すずな (turnip), and すずしろ (daikon radish).

examples.japanese: {一月|いちがつ}{七日|なのか}に{七草|ななくさ}がゆを{食|た}べる。
examples.english: We eat seven-herb rice porridge on January 7th.

examples.japanese: スーパーで{七草|ななくさ}セットを{買|か}ってきた。
examples.english: I bought a seven-herb set at the supermarket.

examples.japanese: {正月|しょうがつ}の{食|た}べすぎで{疲|つか}れた{胃|い}を{休|やす}めるために、{七草|ななくさ}がゆを{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made seven-herb porridge to rest my stomach after overeating during New Year's.

notes:
{七草|ななくさ} usually refers specifically to the {春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven herbs of spring), eaten on January 7th. There is also {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven flowers of autumn), but this is for viewing, not eating.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {七草|ななくさ}がゆ / {七草粥|ななくさがゆ} (seven-herb rice porridge)
- {春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven herbs of spring)
- {秋|あき}の{七草|ななくさ} (seven flowers of autumn)
- {七草|ななくさ}の{節句|せっく} (the seven-herb festival, January 7th)

CULTURAL NOTES:
- The custom of eating {七草|ななくさ}がゆ on January 7th dates back to the Heian period
- It serves both as a prayer for health and as a way to give the stomach a rest after rich New Year's food
- Supermarkets sell pre-packaged {七草|ななくさ} sets in early January
